question: What are the basics of web accessibility? Semantic HTML, labels, keyboard, ARIA?

scenes.sub: Build for people who cannot see, hear, or use a mouse.
scenes.say: Web accessibility. Roughly one in five people has some disability, so this is not a niche. The good news is that most of it comes free if you use the right H T M L.

scenes.head: Think of an audio guide
scenes.say: Think of an audio guide describing your page. If you build a button as a div with a click handler, the guide just says group. No name, no role, and you cannot reach it with the keyboard. Use a real button, and the guide says: Save, button. Pressing enter and space works too. Same look, completely different experience.

scenes.head: Semantic HTML and labels

panels.code:
// bad
Save
// good

scenes.say: A div is not focusable and has no role. A real button gives you focus, keyboard activation, and the right role for free. Inputs need a label, connected with html for and id. A placeholder disappears and is not a label. Images need alt text that says what the image means. Decorative images get an empty alt.

scenes.head: Keyboard and ARIA

panels.code: Delete file?

items.sub: use native HTML if you can

scenes.say: Try using your site with only the Tab key. Focus should move through every control in a sensible order, and you must always see where it is, so never remove the focus outline. Modals need to trap focus and close on escape. ARIA fills gaps native H T M L cannot: role dialog, or aria expanded on a menu button. But the first rule of ARIA is: do not use ARIA if a native element exists.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: Keyboard only, a screen reader, and axe or Lighthouse.
WCAG AA: 4.5 to 1 for normal text.
Describe purpose. Empty alt if decorative.
Clickable divs and outline none with no replacement.
scenes.say: Likely follow-ups. How do you test accessibility? Keyboard only, a screen reader, and automated tools like axe or Lighthouse. Color contrast? W C A G double A asks for four point five to one for normal text. Alt text? Describe purpose, empty if decorative. The common mistake: clickable divs, and removing the focus outline with no replacement.

lines: Semantic HTML first: button, label, headings, alt.
Everything must work with the keyboard, with visible focus.
ARIA only to fill gaps. Test with a screen reader.
scenes.say: Semantic H T M L first: real buttons, labels, headings, and alt text. Everything must work with the keyboard, with visible focus. Use ARIA only to fill gaps, and test with a screen reader.
